findings.message: Last round's fix only covered the retry note that arrives through `note`. A failed live check is the same kind of passing failure, and it still locks the button. `checkFailure` (apps/web/lib/chat-outcome.ts) says 'anything else is a passing failure to try again' and returns `{ message: "Couldn't check that just now." }` with no field. The client's own `.catch` at FormConfirm.tsx:34 returns the same message. Both go into `check`, and `blocked = … || Boolean(check?.message)` then disables the confirm button. The only way to clear it is to edit a field, because only an edit runs the check again. Fix: return transient check failures with a flag (or as a notice) that shows the message without blocking the button. Keep blocking for real refusals (schema or propose check, a card no longer open). Also make the client `.catch` use the same rule instead of a second copy of the message.
findings.scenario: The person changes Key to NWP. The live check's DB call times out, so checkCardField returns {message: "Couldn't check that just now."}. The button stays disabled even though nothing is wrong with the input, and the card can't be confirmed without retyping a field.

findings.message: This variant table for the FormChips fix only calls `edited()`, which already trimmed before this round. It passes with or without the fix, so it proves nothing about the defect: the input drew `value.trim()` and used the " " sentinel. Only the e2e covers that, for one case ('Northwind Traders'). Fix: add a component-level test that renders FormChips or FormConfirm, types several multi-word values key by key (including a trailing space mid-typing and a value equal to a listed option), and checks the input's shown value. It must fail when the old `value.trim()` and sentinel are put back.
findings.scenario: Put back `value={value.trim()}` and `onChange(e.target.value || " ")` in FormChips.tsx. All three rows of the 'typed client of several words' table still pass.
